notes: Both evals run against a model that ALREADY EXISTS. That is deliberate: the failure mode this skill is most likely to have in the field is not producing a bad first cut, it is destroying a good one on the second run. The fixture carries four traps a careful reader can reach and one — the delta-merge — that only shows up under a re-run.

evals.name: capability-vs-context
evals.prompt: Our architect is pushing to give Routing its own service and its own team. Before we commit, is Routing actually a bounded context? Repo: <fixture>, model in docs/domain.
evals.expected_output: The capability-vs-context test applied to Routing with evidence from the model, and a proposal — not an applied change.
assertions: The capability-vs-context test is actually applied, not just referenced
Routing's empty aggregate list and its own note ('owns no rule of its own') are cited as the evidence
The verdict is that Routing decides nothing of its own, so it is a capability or a pass-through rather than a boundary
The one rule that lands on Routing's moment — no hand-over before the declaration is submitted — is identified as belonging to a context that can enforce it
The change is written as a proposal; no file under the fixture's docs/domain is modified
The team/service question is answered as a consequence of the boundary, not as an org preference

evals.name: delta-merge-not-overwrite
evals.prompt: We've just won a contract for temperature-controlled freight — cold chain. Reefer containers have a temperature range that has to hold from depot to depot, and a breach has to be logged and the customer told. Update our domain model for it. Repo: <fixture>, docs/domain. Note that a few of those model.yaml files have hand-written notes in them from the planner that we want kept.
evals.expected_output: A delta merged into the existing model — new concepts added, existing ids and human notes preserved, anything dropped flagged.
assertions: Existing context and aggregate ids are preserved; nothing is renumbered or renamed silently
The hand-written notes in the fixture's model.yaml files survive the update verbatim
The new cold-chain concepts are added as a delta rather than by rewriting the files wholesale
Whether cold chain is a new bounded context or an extension of an existing one is argued, not assumed
Anything the update drops or supersedes is flagged explicitly rather than disappearing
The temperature-breach rule is not invented into an invariant beyond what the prompt states, and what is unknown stays unknown with the person who could answer it named
